query:
title: Go breaking-change review prerequisites

question: Hi team, my ARM specification change is ready for Go SDK breaking-change review, but ARM signoff is still pending. I need the Go approval label to move forward. What should I do next?
ground_truth: ARM signoff and Go SDK breaking-change approval are separate decisions. Complete the applicable review prerequisites, including the pending ARM signoff, before requesting final Go approval. Share the generated Go SDK diff and compatibility impact with the Go reviewers so they can assess the change. Passing validation alone does not establish approval; the approval label must come from an authorized reviewer.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

testcase: Go development-branch suppression is not release approval
query:
title: Go development-branch suppression

question: We're making an ARM specification change on a development branch for a private preview, and Go SDK validation is flagging breaking changes. If we get suppression approved for this branch, can we use the same approval when we copy the changes to a published release branch?
ground_truth: A development-branch suppression is not blanket approval for a published release. Suppression permits a scoped gate exception; it does not establish SDK compatibility. Confirm the branch policy and the authorized reviewer's decision for the private preview, then have the actual release change and generated Go SDK compatibility reviewed for the release context.

query:
title: Go breaking-change label unrelated to my change

question: My specification change only adds an example, but the Go SDK comparison reports a removed exported field. I think that removal came from another change. What information should I include when I request suppression?
ground_truth: Include the generated Go diff or changelog and the specification versions or commits used by the comparison. Trace the removed field to the change that introduced it and show why your example update is unrelated. An authorized reviewer can then assess a scoped suppression under the applicable process. Do not change the comparison baseline just to hide the failure.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

testcase: Go operation rename preserves HTTP but breaks callers
query:
title: Go operation rename compatibility

question: I renamed my TypeSpec operation from updateTags to update without changing the PATCH URI or method. Our released Go client has UpdateTags, but regeneration now removes it and adds Update. Is this still a breaking change? How can I keep the existing Go method name?
ground_truth: Yes. Removing UpdateTags breaks Go callers even though the HTTP contract is unchanged. In client.tsp, apply a Go-scoped client name to the current TypeSpec operation, for example @@clientName(update, "updateTags", "go"), qualified with your namespace as needed. Regenerate and confirm UpdateTags remains in the public Go API. Wire compatibility and SDK source compatibility require separate review.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

testcase: Go wire-contract bug fix versus preserved fiction
query:
title: Go boolean property spec correction

question: We found a response property incorrectly specified as a string enum, although our service has always returned a JSON boolean. Correcting the spec changes the generated Go field from *string to *bool. Should I keep the old string type to avoid breaking our SDK consumers?
ground_truth: Keeping *string may preserve the old Go source shape, but it leaves the SDK unable to decode the actual boolean response correctly. The wire-contract correction and the exported Go type change are separate concerns: the latter still breaks callers. Review affected releases and consumers with the Go owners to choose a valid mitigation or versioning approach. A spec bug fix does not automatically grant SDK breaking-change approval.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

query:
title: Extensible SKU values in TypeSpec

question: I'm defining an Azure API SKU as enum Sku { Small, Large }, but we expect more string values in the future. How should I model this in TypeSpec, and will changing it affect our released Go SDK?
ground_truth: Use an extensible union with named string literals and the string scalar, for example union Sku { Small: "Small", Large: "Large", string }. Azure core's no-enum guidance favors this representation for values that can grow; version enums are a separate allowed use. Compare the regenerated Go API against the released SDK and review any compatibility changes independently. The recommended TypeSpec shape does not itself approve an SDK break.

testcase: Go green checks with blocking review comment
query:
title: Go SDK merge readiness

question: My generated Go SDK change has passed all required checks and has no merge conflicts. A reviewer still has a blocking comment about a public field name. Can I merge it now, or is there something else I need to do?
ground_truth: The blocking review comment still needs to be resolved before merge. Correct the name in the appropriate source or client customization, regenerate if needed, and ask the reviewer to confirm the resolution. Green CI and a conflict-free branch do not replace review approval.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

query:
title: Preserve released Go field names

question: Our stable Go model has fields named ToBsuid and FromBsuid. After I cleaned up the specification, regeneration changed their casing, but the wire property names stayed the same. Can we accept the new names, or should I preserve the released fields?
ground_truth: Preserve the released Go field names. Renaming an exported stable field is a source-compatibility change even when its wire name is unchanged. Apply Go-scoped client naming customizations to the underlying TypeSpec properties, regenerate, and inspect the compatibility diff. Naming cleanup on an unreleased API is a different situation.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

testcase: Go review handoff without owner identity
query:
title: Go SDK review handoff

question: My generated Go SDK change has passed the required checks, and all blocking review comments are resolved. I'm not sure who owns the final Go approval. Who should I contact next?
ground_truth: Follow up with the requested Go reviewers or the matching CODEOWNERS for the affected package. Final approval must come from an authorized human reviewer. The information here does not identify an individual owner; check the actual review requests and ownership file rather than guessing a person's handle.

query:
title: Preserve Go naming customization

question: A reviewer asked me to correct acronym casing in our generated Go SDK. I edited the .go file, but regeneration overwrote my change. Where should I make the naming fix so it survives regeneration?
ground_truth: Put the fix in the supported specification or client customization layer, not only in generated .go output. For TypeSpec, use a Go-scoped client name on the relevant source symbol where appropriate, then regenerate and check the resulting name. If the symbol is already released, preserve compatibility and review any public rename with the Go owners.

expected_references.title: Go SDK breaking-change review and resolution

query:
title: Go generation cannot find serialized type field

question: My SDK generation fails while processing a response example with "field with serializedName 'type' not found in model 'ArmConnectionResponse'". My TypeSpec model inherits from a tracked ARM resource. What should I check to fix this?
ground_truth: This points to a mismatch between the example's serialized response shape and the model being processed. Compare the emitted Swagger model with the referenced example, including inherited fields and visibility, and check the generator version and configuration. Please share the emitted model, full example, and detailed generation log if the mismatch is unclear. Inheritance alone is not enough to identify a particular decorator or field deletion as the fix.

expected_references.title: SDK validation artifacts and detailed errors

query:
title: Go SDK validation repository checkout failure

question: My validation log says "failed to get sdk repo: core.repositoryformatversion does not support extension: worktreeconfig", followed by "Failed to read generateOutput.json". Other teams are seeing the same checkout error for unrelated services. Is there anything I need to change in my API model?
ground_truth: The first failure is in repository checkout and Git tooling, not an API model diagnostic. The missing generateOutput.json is likely a consequence of generation never starting successfully. Share the detailed logs and run context with the engineering-system owners and check for a shared tooling or Git compatibility issue. Retry after the infrastructure problem is resolved; changing the model is not supported by this evidence.

expected_references.title: SDK validation artifacts and detailed errors

testcase: Go APIView name versus revision approval
query:
title: Go APIView revision blocks release

question: Our package name is already marked First Release Approved, and my SDK change has merged. The release check still says the newly generated GA APIView revision is missing API approval. Why is it blocked, and what approval do I need?
ground_truth: Package-name or first-release approval is separate from approval of the exact APIView revision used by the release. Ask the authorized API reviewer to review that revision, resolve its blocking comments, and approve it. Merging the SDK change or having an earlier revision approved does not satisfy the new revision's gate.

testcase: Go release success needs registry evidence
query:
title: Go package publication verification

question: I've triggered the release pipeline for our Go module. How can I tell whether the version is actually published and ready for customers to use?
ground_truth: Check the matching release run for successful completion of the publishing steps, then verify the exact module path and version are available to Go consumers. For example, resolve module@version with go get and check the corresponding version on pkg.go.dev. Triggering the pipeline alone does not prove publication, so the release remains unconfirmed until you have that evidence.

query:
title: Go dependency allowlist exception

question: Our new Go SDK module needs a native binary distribution module outside azure-sdk-for-go, but I don't see it in the repository dependency instruction. We've proposed an exception. Can I merge the dependency change, or does the exception need a separate review?
ground_truth: The proposed exception needs owner review before you rely on it. Check the current go.mod standards and any applicable package-specific exceptions, then have the owners review both the dependency and the policy change, including compatibility and maintenance implications. A proposal is not an approved exception, but that does not mean every external dependency is prohibited.

testcase: Go module deprecation versus immediate deletion
query:
title: Deprecating a Go SDK module

question: Our service is retiring, and there isn't a replacement for its Go SDK module. Can we delete the module now, or do we need to publish a deprecation release first? What should I include?
ground_truth: Follow the Go module deprecation process rather than treating retirement as permission for immediate deletion. Prepare the appropriate final patch with a // Deprecated: module comment in go.mod, a changelog notice, and README guidance. State clearly that there is no replacement. Deprecation, retraction, and deletion are different actions; confirm removal timing with the applicable lifecycle policy and owners.

testcase: Go spec merge does not prove SDK release
query:
title: New API version available to Go consumers

question: Our ARM specification change for a new API version has merged, but we haven't generated or released the Go SDK yet. Can our customers use that API version through the existing Go module? What do we need to do next?
ground_truth: The spec merge does not make the new API version available through an updated Go SDK. Generate the management-plane SDK for the desired version, complete validation and review, release it, and verify publication. Use the Azure SDK Tools Agent lifecycle workflow where applicable. Do not assume SDK generation or release happened automatically when the specification merged.

testcase: Go language feature does not prove minimum version policy
query:
title: Raising a Go SDK minimum language version

question: We want to use generic methods in a new major version of our Go SDK. I've heard a future Go release will support them. Can we raise the minimum version in go.mod and stop supporting older Go versions?
ground_truth: First verify whether generic methods are supported in an actually released compiler using the authoritative Go language and release documentation. A future feature proposal does not establish that support. Separately review the minimum-version change, supported consumers, and compatibility policy with the SDK owners. A major release or one package's exception is not a universal policy for dropping older Go versions.
